observations: A roughly rectangular white line border frames the composition, with jagged breaks at the corners and loose overrun strokes extending beyond it into the dark brown field.
Two oval eye forms sit side by side in the upper-center area, each filled with dense crossed black lines; a small open-mouthed form with visible tooth shapes sits lower and centered.
Red lines run vertically and diagonally across the background and through the face structure, layered beneath white outlines and above the muted brown-grey tonal fill.
reading: The white lines trace a face-like structure—brow ridge, eye sockets, nose bridge, open mouth—but the forms stay loose, collapsing into the dark ground rather than resolving. Crossed marks inside the eye shapes read as blocked or sealed. The red lines underneath sit agitated against the heavy brown, and the whole image lands closer to unease than calm.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between #58 and #60 in both title and recorded order. Where #58 opens into pale greys, yellows and soft tonal circles, #59 pulls back to near-monochrome brown with red as the only strong accent.

connections.reason: Both use white lines to trace a face structure over a layered ground, but #58 opens into pale greys, yellows and soft circles while #59 closes into dark brown and red—a direct contrast in color key.

Both #59 and #60 use a rectangular border line that breaks and overruns at the edges, but #60 spreads into multicolor line density against white while #59 keeps its marks compressed inside a dark field.

lookingQuestion: What happens to the white border lines at the corners—do they close the face in or leave a way out?
ambiguities: The brown-grey tonal fill beneath the line work may be a separate layer or blended strokes; the image alone cannot confirm which.
The nnotb #98 comparison image shows a flat silhouette figure on a teal ground with no structural overlap with #59; no useful formal connection was found and it was excluded.
